reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports spray-coating and low friction/wear at room temperature under high load for a steel substrate, but provides no data on high-temperature performance, tribofilm stability up to 800 °C, or behavior on a CoCrFeNi substrate. E2 shows failure in water, highlighting solvent sensitivity, but does not address the key premise of wide-temperature effectiveness. Thus, the critical premises regarding high-temperature tribofilm stability and performance on CoCrFeNi are unsupported.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 can be applied by air spray coating
These nanoflakes exhibit stress-induced tribocatalytic activity that facilitates self-lubrication in ambient conditions
The tribocatalytic activity promotes formation of a low-shear tribofilm that reduces friction and wear
This tribofilm remains effective and stable across a wide temperature range from RT to 800 °C
The coating will reduce friction and wear of CoCrFeNi alloy across the full temperature range
